body:
## Problem

`$ --stop <uuid>` on a detached docker execution runs a plain `docker stop <container>`. Docker's default grace period is **10 seconds**, then the process gets `SIGKILL`. A program that does real cleanup on `SIGTERM` (commit work, upload a log, post a status comment) is killed in the middle of it. The caller has no way to pass a longer grace period.

Code (commit e4077847a1d52e3f727103b374b0687569ad45cd):

- JS: `js/src/lib/execution-control.js` → `args: ['stop', sessionName]`
- Rust: `rust/src/lib/execution_control.rs` → `args: vec!["stop".to_string(), session_name.to_string()]`

## Evidence (public)

Hive Mind ran a `solve` session for https://github.com/link-foundation/link-cli/pull/175 in a detached docker execution. It was stopped with `$ --stop <uuid>`. From the session log ([excerpt in hive-mind](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-4048-03e6079741e9/docs/case-studies/issue-4048/data/public-link-cli-pr175-monitoring.log)):

```
[interrupt] +1ms handler entered
⚠️  Session interrupted by user (CTRL+C)
...
[interrupt] +135ms log-upload: start
📈 [RESOURCES] phase=log_upload_start ts=2026-11-12T04%3A52%3A24.391Z ...
  📎 Uploading log using gh-upload-log...      (41MB log)

=== Container post-mortem ===
Exit Code:  137 (SIGKILL - 128+9)
OOMKilled:  false
FinishedAt: 2026-11-12T04:52:34.453264659Z
```

The handler starts at 04:52:24.39Z. `SIGKILL` comes 10.06 s later, which is exactly Docker's default `docker stop` timeout. The 41 MB log upload never finished.

## Reproduction

```sh
# a command that needs 30 s to shut down cleanly
$ --isolated docker --detached -- sh -c 'trap "echo cleanup-start; sleep 30; echo cleanup-done; exit 0" TERM; while :; do sleep 1; done'
$ --stop <uuid>
$ --status <uuid>     # exit code 137, "cleanup-done" never printed
```

## Workaround

Stop the container yourself with a longer grace period, e.g. `docker stop -t 120 <container>`, instead of `$ --stop <uuid>`. Or make the program finish cleanup in under 10 s, which is not possible for large uploads.

## Suggested fix

1. Add a stop timeout option. Either:
   - `$ --stop <uuid> --stop-timeout <seconds>` → `docker stop -t <seconds> <container>`; or
   - accept `--stop-timeout <seconds>` at launch and pass it to `docker run --stop-timeout`, so a plain `docker stop` honors it too.
   An environment default (e.g. `START_DOCKER_STOP_TIMEOUT`) would let callers like Hive Mind set it once.
2. Print the grace period in the stop message, e.g. `Requested graceful stop (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 10s)`. That makes the 10 s cut-off visible.
3. Make the same change in JS and Rust, and add a test that asserts the `-t` argument in the generated control command.
title: --stop on docker executions uses docker's default 10s grace period; allow a configurable stop timeout
